items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Vernon Andrade's Andratti's was the house band always at the Renaissance Ballroom... and he was the banjo player in the band.

ctx.x: Vernon Andrade's Andratti's orchestra possibly working under the name Dixie Stompers.

No, that's incorrect, 1000 percent incorrect. Vernon Andrade's Andratti's was the house band always at the Renaissance Ballroom at 138th and 7th Avenue in New York City, and he played for different club dates. This was all he did, and he was the banjo player in the band. And the leader -- and he had a regular group there that played all these things, all these jobs with him, and his band didn't record, and they went under the same name of -- as Vernon Andrade Andratti's and his Renaissance Ballroom Band.

Uh-huh. I see. Okay. Here we have Horace Henderson's Wilberforce Collegians, which we've talked about, sometimes billed as Fletcher Henderson's Stompers. Now it says here, "Basically, Horace's college band with Rex Stewart, Benny Carter, Freddy Jenkins, et cetera, about 1925 to spring, 1928." I remember asking you about this before, and you said that the Stompers was a name that was used for recording purposes.
